messages:
amanda: Kicking off the POC with Finch Health today — they want to validate streaming SDK + function/tool calls and reliably emit structured JSON (medical-summary schema). Can we confirm recommended SDK flow and any gotchas?
raj: Congrats team. Main asks? latency SLOs? residency? sample throughput?
amanda: They want sub-150ms p95 for short prompts (<= 128 tokens) and burst to 120 qps in EU region. Data must remain in eu-west-1, and they ask about KMS for PHI keys.
ben_eng: For sub-150ms p95, use Dedicated with reserved capacity; hosted can hit it but depends on noisy neighbors. Recommend model: redwood-v2-small-quant for throughput, or a slightly larger variant if quality matters.
sara_se: On KMS: Private deployment supports customer KMS/HSM. For Hosted we support envelope encryption with customer KMS in a partner account — we'll need SOC2 appendix.
amanda: Good. On the streaming SDK: they want to call a function mid-stream and have the runtime emit a structured tool call then continue streaming the function result back into the chat. Any example?
ben_eng: Yep. SDK pattern: open stream, stream tokens until model emits a tool call event, pause user-stream, perform the tool, then send tool-result as user/system message and resume. Pseudocode:```python
with client.stream_chat(model="redwood-v2-small") as s:
    for evt in s:
        if evt.type == "tool_call":
            # evt.data has name + args (JSON)
            result = run_tool(evt.data)
            s.send_system_message("tool_result", payload=result)
        else:
            print(evt.token, end="")```
raj: How do we ensure the function args are validated against Finch's schema? They want strict typing to avoid hallucinated tool calls.
ben_eng: Recommend supplying a JSON schema in the request: pass `structured_schema` param — runtime will validate and reject/flag anything nonconforming. Also set `max_tool_retries=0` so model can't repeatedly hallucinate.
sara_se: Add rate limits on tool execution on the adapter side to avoid cost spikes. Also recommend signing ephemeral creds for the adapter (STS) and rotating every 15m.
amanda: Pricing ask: they want a ballpark cost for 120 qps sustained with 128 token responses on Dedicated reserved vs hosted on-demand.
ben_eng: Ballpark: Hosted on-demand ~ $0.0008/token (example) — at 120 qps * 128 tokens * 3600s ~ $$$ per hour. Dedicated reserved depends on instance type; give them 1–2 A100-equivalents for that qps; committed monthly ~ discounted ~40%. I'll run numbers and post a spreadsheet.
raj: Can we do a quick canary showing streaming tool-call flow? If ops-bot can spin a test endpoint.
ops-bot: deploy started: canary-runtime/redwood-canary-eu — logs at https://ci.internal/builds/3245612345
amanda: Test notes: initial canary showed 2 tool-call events, 1 malformed args due to edge-case in our JSON schema (optional fields missing).
ben_eng: Fix: make optional fields explicit on schema (use `nullable` or default empty string). Also enable `validate_on_emit=true` in the SDK to catch earlier.
sara_se: Security questionnaire item: "Where is PII persisted?" Response: ephemeral KV cache on nodes, 0 retention in control plane by default, customer can opt-in for audit logs stored in their bucket (S3/EU region) with CMK. I'll draft wording.
amanda: Next steps: 1) ben to send perf/cost estimate spreadsheet by EOD 2) sara to draft security Q responses + SOC2 appendix pointer 3) raj to run canary with schema fixes and post logs 4) amanda to schedule demo with Finch for Tue 10am CET.
ben_eng: on it — I'll include a sample load config and recommended Dedicated sizing.
raj: I'll re-run the canary after schema update and post the trimmed logs + timing numbers.
amanda: Thanks all. If anyone wants to join the Tuesday demo prep sync, ping me. :thumbsup:
